newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran plans more Caspian oil, gas exploration - MEE.
newsitem.headline: Iran plans more Caspian oil, gas exploration - MEE.

text.p: Iran's National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) is planning further oil and gas exploration at three wells in the Iranian offshore portion of the Caspian Sea, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) said on Monday.

MEES said that based on an interview it conducted with Seyed Mehdi Hosseini, NIOC's director for exploration, work was continuing at the three wells which have so far been drilled by the company in the area -- Khazar No. 1, Meghdad No. 1 and Meysam No.1.
He said better yields could be achieved at Khazar No. 1, drilled in 1989-91 to a total depth of 5,570 metres, with a new drilling location.

He added that NIOC had improved information due to fresh seismic data acquisition and prospects for the area, located in the western part of Iran's Caspian zone, some 25 km northwest of Bandar Anzali, are seen as good.
Hosseini said the existing 2-D data acquisition will probably be followed up by 3-D seismic work.
He said the original target of the second wildcat, Meghdad No. 1, located in the southeastern part of the Caspian, some 50 km northwest of the Neka terminal, had been a depth of 4,500 metres.
But the company decided to go deeper after the rig design had been modified to reach 6,000 metres rather than 4,500 metres, he added.
He said testing was difficult due to high pressures, but the company eventually found traces of hydrocarbons, and that after data collection, it was closed at a depth of 5,760 metres.
The well was spudded in September 1995, he said.
NIOC spudded the third wildcat -- Meysam No. 1 -- located about five km northeast of Meghdad No. 1, in June 1996.
Drilling had now reached around 3,000 metres and is continuing towards the target depth of 4,500 metres, Hosseini said.
NIOC has recently completed 11,000 kms of seismic covering areas with water depths of less than 200 metres, in addition to the 6,000 kms shot in 1991-92 and 7,000 kms done earlier, he said.

He added that the focus for drilling might now move back to the western side of the Caspian offshore, given that chances for success would rise due to better seismic data and selection of drilling locations, MEES reported.
There are currently six seismic teams working in Iran -- four onshore and two offshore -- with onshore work focused on areas in southwestern near the Iraqi border, central Iran and in the northeast.
